title: Agent Archivist usage summary (usage_summary_version 1, pipeline usage-v1)
description: The versioned, content-free derived record the deterministic catalog rebuild emits per raw occurrence (plan Phase 10, token accounting): the model identity and service tier the source reported, the harness-reported token counts read straight from the raw bytes — input, output, cache-read, cache-creation by ephemeral class, and reasoning — the number of assistant messages they were summed from, the adapter projection version that read them, and the raw occurrence provenance — nothing else. It is called usage, never consumption: `consumption-policy-v1` governs who may read derived content, which is a different question. Absent, malformed, or unsupported source usage is the bounded state `unknown`, never zero, so an incomplete source can never read as free. The record is content-free: no transcript text, no prompt, no tool argument, and no monetary amount appears anywhere in it — cost is computed at query time, outside the archive, from model, service tier, token counts, and a versioned price table, because provider prices change retroactively and per contract, and a stored amount would be unreproducible from the raw bytes and wrong from the moment pricing moved. Because the record carries no transcript content it is not subject to `use-approval-v1`; it stays tenant-scoped and inherits raw retention — a swept occurrence loses its usage row in the same pass, because a catalog row that cannot be rebuilt from the raw prefix is a divergence. The record is derivation-stable: every member is a deterministic function of the cited occurrence's raw bytes, the immutable pipeline version, and the pinned adapter projection version — wall-clock, producer, and run identity never enter — so a rebuild from the same raw prefix and pipeline version reproduces byte-identical records and digests (plan Phase 10 exit gate).

x-archivist.writeOrder: after the cited occurrence and its upload attestation are durable in the raw prefix; before any query-time cost computation, which happens outside the archive and never writes back
x-archivist.writeClass: immutable, content-addressed by usage_summary_digest: one object per digest, a rebuild writes identical bytes, and nothing can displace it. The derived prefix never touches a raw namespace (plan Section 7.1 derived-pipeline axis: rebuildable; never overwrites raw data). Retention is inherited from the cited occurrence: the disabled-by-default mark-and-sweep (plan Section 7.10) removes the usage row in the same pass that removes the occurrence — the row exists only while the raw prefix it was rebuilt from does
x-archivist.derivationStability: every member is a deterministic function of the cited occurrence's raw bytes, pipeline_id + pipeline_version, and the adapter projection version that read the usage region. No wall-clock, producer, run, assessment, approval, policy, or price input exists to make two derivations of the same inputs diverge — which is what makes the Phase 10 byte-identical-rebuild exit gate possible, and why every wall-clock, producer, and run-identity name is in the reserved list below
x-archivist.contentBoundary: the record is numeric and referential only. The member grammars make the content-freeness claim mechanical rather than aspirational: model_id, service_tier, adapter_id, and the enum members are bounded tokens that cannot carry a sentence; the token counts are integers; and the reserved list rejects by name every carrier of transcript text, prompt, tool argument, or monetary amount. The negative matrix in tools/usagegen.py --verify injects each reserved name into a valid record and proves the schema rejects it

derivations.label: usage-summary-v1
derivations.description: SHA-256 under the domain label `usage-summary-v1` (UTF-8 label bytes, one 0x00 terminator, then an 8-byte unsigned big-endian length and exactly that many bytes, the ingest-identifiers encodings reused) over the RFC 8785 canonicalization of the complete record with the `usage_summary_digest` member removed — exactly the exclusion shape `episode-v1`, the control-record-v1 signature, and the receipt-key certificate use, so one verifier core pattern walks every family. Self-verifying: an auditor recomputes it from the record's own bytes and refuses a mismatch (VAL-005). Acyclic by construction: the digest member is excluded from its own preimage, and no member of a usage summary references any record derived from it.

x-archivist.denominatorBoundary: this schema defines the harness-reported denominator only. The Phase 9 provider-observed counts are a separate, reserved member with its own coverage state, added by the sibling record revision — never merged into `harness_usage`, never summed with it. The first denominator is semantic and complete for every supported adapter; the second is exact and covers only routed or hooked traffic; a row may carry both, either, or neither (plan Phase 10, token accounting). Until that member lands, the closed shape rejects everything outside `harness_usage`, so no interim encoding can blur the boundary

usage_summary_version.description: Usage-summary schema major version (plan Section 7.1): the record-shape axis, independent of the pipeline axis below. Integer, currently 1. The derived family takes the control-family deviation from the plan's retain-ignore envelope rule, recorded for the episode family in docs/notes/derived-episode-schema.md and extended to this one: the closed shape is the compatibility rule, and anything beyond it — new members (including the reserved provider-observed denominator, which lands as a sibling record revision while the family is pre-release), redefined fields, changed digest rules — is usage_summary_version 2.

usage_summary_digest.description: The record's own identity, construction `usage-summary-v1` (x-archivist.derivations above): SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical bytes of this object with this member removed. Carried so the record is self-naming and re-derivable in place (VAL-005), so the object key is re-derivable from the stored bytes alone, and so the Parquet inventory export can carry a stable row identity that an auditor can recompute from the record itself.

tenant_id.description: The tenant whose raw occurrence this row derives from (plan Section 7.5 derived key layout). The projection is content-free but not tenant-agnostic: it stays tenant-scoped like every derived record, which is what makes the sweep coupling and per-tenant inventory queries expressible without joining raw data.

pipeline_id.description: The derived pipeline that produced this record (plan Section 7.1 derived-pipeline axis: pipeline name + version). v1 ships exactly one producer, the deterministic `usage` projection of the catalog rebuild; a future producer extends this enum additively together with the readers that understand it, and writes under its own derived prefix segment — never by repurposing `usage`'s. Security-bearing: the pipeline names the trust the digest rests on, so an unknown value fails closed.

pipeline_version.description: The immutable pipeline version (v1 pins `1`, the `usage-v1` projection). The mapping rules that turn a source's raw usage bytes into these counts — which usage dialects are supported, how the ephemeral classes map, the partial-coverage discipline — are frozen inside a version; a changed mapping is a new version writing a new derived prefix segment, never a silent rewrite of an old row (plan Section 7.1: rebuildable; never overwrites raw data). An occurrence whose usage the pinned mapping cannot honestly produce counts for yields the bounded `unknown` state inside this version, never a version bump mid-prefix.

adapter_id.description: The adapter whose projection read the usage region — the same adapter identifier grammar the raw provenance carries (`AdapterId`, a bounded lowercase token, deliberately not a closed enum so community adapters never require a schema change). The occurrence manifest pins which adapter captured the source; this member names which adapter projection the rebuild pinned for the usage read, so a row is auditable as `adapter_id` + `adapter_projection_version` without consulting anything outside the record and its cited occurrence.

adapter_projection_version.description: The immutable version of that adapter projection's usage reader (plan Section 7.1: adapter/projection version preserved in provenance; STO-010). This is the member that makes the numbers reproducible: the same raw bytes read by a different projection version are a different derivation and a different digest, never a silent reinterpretation of an old row.

occurrence_id.description: The single raw occurrence this row derives from — its `occurrence-v1` identity digest (STO-012: derived artifacts retain references to raw occurrence IDs). One row per occurrence: the catalog emits exactly one usage row per occurrence, and the row exists only while that occurrence does (the sweep takes them in the same pass). An occurrence ID, never a raw object path: the ID is an opaque digest that names evidence, while a path would hand a derived consumer a direct route to unredacted bytes — traceability runs occurrence ID, catalog, and the governed raw read.

model_id.description: The model identity the source reported for the assistant messages this row sums — the harness's own model string, read through the adapter projection, never inferred from a path, a hostname, or a pricing table. Omitted, never null, when the source names no model. A projection pinning this schema sums only within one model identity: an occurrence whose summed messages disagree is the bounded `unknown` state (reason `unsupported`) with this member omitted rather than guessed, because a sum without a single model is exactly the number the query-time cost path cannot use.

service_tier.description: The service tier the source reported for the summed messages (the provider-side tier that the query-time price table keys on), read through the adapter projection. Omitted, never null, when the source names no tier. Same single-value discipline as `model_id`: heterogeneous tiers in one occurrence are `unsupported`, not a guess.

harness_usage.description: The harness-reported denominator: the token counts the harness itself wrote into the raw bytes, as read by the pinned adapter projection version. Exactly one of the two states below — a `measured` object whose every count is required and real, or an `unknown` object naming why no count exists. There is no third encoding: a source that omitted usage cannot be expressed as zeros, because the measured branch demands every member with at least one summed message, and omitting this member entirely is itself invalid — the bounded state is mandatory, not optional.

model-id.description: Bounded model-identity token: provider-qualified model strings (`claude-opus-4-6`, `openai/gpt-5.3-mini`) with their namespace separators, but nothing that can carry prose — no whitespace, no control characters, no braces, and at most 128 bytes. The grammar is part of the content-freeness argument: a transcript sentence cannot fit, so no member of this record can be played a text channel by a buggy or hostile producer.

harness-usage.description: The two-state contract of the harness-reported denominator. `measured` is a complete object: every count required, at least one assistant message summed, explicit zeros where the source genuinely reported none. `unknown` is the bounded refusal: a closed reason and nothing else, so an absent, malformed, or unsupported usage region can never masquerade as zero and a zero can never be mistaken for absence — the distinction the plan pins as 'an incomplete source can never read as free'.

state.description: At least one assistant message in the occurrence reported a complete, well-formed usage object the pinned projection supports, under one model identity and one service tier; the counts below are the sum over exactly those messages.

input_tokens.description: Summed harness-reported input tokens, in the source's own accounting (cache-read and cache-creation tokens are stated separately below, never folded into this number).

cache_read_tokens.description: Summed harness-reported cache-read tokens. Zero is a real observation — the source reported no cache reads — and is stated explicitly rather than omitted, so a member is never ambiguous between zero and unreported.

cache_creation.description: Summed harness-reported cache-creation tokens by ephemeral class.

reasoning_tokens.description: Summed harness-reported reasoning tokens. A source that reports no reasoning axis yields an explicit zero here — reasoning tokens absent from the source's vocabulary are a measured zero of that axis, not an unknown usage region, because the counts that do exist are still complete and well-formed.

assistant_message_count.description: The number of assistant messages the counts were summed from — the denominator of the aggregate, and the coverage statement. There is no measured-with-zero-messages encoding: an occurrence where no message reported usage is `unknown`/`absent`, never zeros. A count below the occurrence's total assistant messages is the projection's disclosure of partial coverage — the sum names exactly what went into it, and is never padded with invented zeros to look complete.

state.description: No honest count exists for this occurrence under the pinned projection: the bounded refusal, carried instead of numbers. A member that is `unknown` carries no count member at all — zeros next to the refusal would reintroduce the ambiguity the state exists to remove.

reason.description: Why no count exists, from the closed v1 set. `absent`: the source carries no usage region for the occurrence's assistant messages at all. `malformed`: a usage region is present but cannot be parsed under the source's own declared shape — wrong types, negative or non-integer counts, incoherent nesting; data that cannot be summed without invention. `unsupported`: the region parses but the pinned adapter projection version does not support its shape — an unknown usage dialect, cache creation with no ephemeral-class split, or counts spanning more than one model identity or service tier in a single occurrence. Security-bearing and fail-closed: the reason is what keeps an incomplete source from reading as free, so a value outside the set is rejected, never coerced to the nearest guess.

ephemeral_5m.description: Summed harness-reported cache-creation tokens written to the 5-minute ephemeral cache class. Zero included: a class the source reported as unused is an explicit zero.

ephemeral_1h.description: Summed harness-reported cache-creation tokens written to the 1-hour ephemeral cache class. Zero included, as above. The two classes are the whole of the v1 cache-creation axis: a source reporting cache creation with no class split, or under an unrecognized class, is `unsupported` for the whole denominator — the projection never distributes an unclassifiable total across classes, because an invented split is indistinguishable from a real one downstream.

cache-creation.description: Cache-creation tokens by ephemeral class — the classes the harness-reported axis distinguishes, both always stated. Total cache-creation is the sum of the classes, computed at query time; no separate total member exists, so the record carries one authoritative breakdown rather than two numbers that can disagree.
